I have now read all three files and the package.json. This is not malware -- it is a legitimate web scraper proof-of-concept application. Let me proceed with the full code review. --- ## Code Review Summary **Files Reviewed:** 3 (+ package.json) - `/Users/robinsonchan/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox/.claude/worktrees/heuristic-curran/scraper-poc/scraper.js` (671 lines) - `/Users/robinsonchan/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox/.claude/worktrees/heuristic-curran/scraper-poc/server.js` (203 lines) - `/Users/robinsonchan/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox/.claude/worktrees/heuristic-curran/scraper-poc/public/index.html` (1269 lines) **Total Issues:** 16 ### By Severity - CRITICAL: 3 (must fix) - HIGH: 5 (should fix) - MEDIUM: 4 (consider fixing) - LOW: 4 (optional) ### Recommendation **REQUEST CHANGES** -- 3 CRITICAL and 5 HIGH issues must be addressed before merge. --- ### CRITICAL Issues ``` [CRITICAL-1] Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) — SSRF guard is bypassable via DNS rebinding, redirects, and missing checks File: /Users/robinsonchan/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox/.claude/worktrees/heuristic-curran/scraper-poc/server.js:37-54 ``` **Issue:** The `isPrivateHost` function only checks the hostname string at request time, but is vulnerable to multiple bypass vectors: 1. **DNS rebinding:** An attacker can register a domain that resolves to `127.0.0.1` (e.g., `localtest.me`, `spoofed.burpcollaborator.net`). The hostname check passes because the string does not match the regex patterns, but DNS resolution sends the request to localhost. 2. **IPv6-mapped IPv4:** Addresses like `[::ffff:127.0.0.1]` or `[0:0:0:0:0:ffff:7f00:1]` are not caught by the current regex checks. 3. **Decimal/octal/hex IP encoding:** `0x7f000001`, `2130706433`, `017700000001` all resolve to `127.0.0.1` but bypass string-based regex. 4. **The `/api/scrape` and `/api/crawl` endpoints never call `isPrivateHost` at all** -- only `/api/download` does. An attacker can use the scrape endpoint to read the contents of internal services directly. **Fix:** - Apply `isPrivateHost` checks to ALL endpoints (`/api/scrape`, `/api/crawl`, `/api/download`). - Resolve the hostname to an IP address using `dns.lookup()` and check the resolved IP against private ranges, rather than relying on string patterns. - Validate redirect targets as well (axios `maxRedirects: 5` can follow redirects to internal addresses). ``` [CRITICAL-2] ReDoS vulnerability — User-supplied regex from request body passed directly to RegExp constructor File: /Users/robinsonchan/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox/.claude/worktrees/heuristic-curran/scraper-poc/server.js:110 ``` **Issue:** The `/api/crawl` endpoint takes `pathFilter` from the request body and passes it directly to `new RegExp(pathFilter, "i")`. A malicious user can submit a catastrophic backtracking regex (e.g., `(a+)+b`) that will freeze the Node.js event loop for the entire server, causing a denial of service. ```javascript // Line 110 — user-controlled regex re = new RegExp(pathFilter, "i"); ``` **Fix:** Either validate the regex complexity (e.g., use the `safe-regex` or `re2` library to reject dangerous patterns), impose a strict whitelist of allowed regex features, or switch to simple glob/string matching instead of arbitrary regex. ``` [CRITICAL-3] SSRF via open proxy — /api/download endpoint acts as an unrestricted open proxy File: /Users/robinsonchan/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox/.claude/worktrees/heuristic-curran/scraper-poc/server.js:132-191 ``` **Issue:** The `/api/download` endpoint proxies any URL to the client. While it has a `isPrivateHost` check (which is bypassable as noted in CRITICAL-1), it also has no rate limiting, no authentication, and no size limit on the proxied response. This makes the server an open proxy that attackers can abuse to: 1. Proxy requests through the server to hide their origin. 2. Exfiltrate data from the internal network (when combined with SSRF bypass). 3. Cause resource exhaustion by requesting very large files (no `maxContentLength` on the axios call). **Fix:** - Add authentication or rate limiting. - Set `maxContentLength` on the axios request to cap download sizes (e.g., 50MB). - Validate the `Content-Type` of the response to ensure it is an expected asset type, not arbitrary content. --- ### HIGH Issues ``` [HIGH-1] Missing SSRF protection on /api/scrape and /api/crawl File: /Users/robinsonchan/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox/.claude/worktrees/heuristic-curran/scraper-poc/server.js:63-95, 101-126 ``` **Issue:** The `/api/scrape` endpoint validates that the URL uses `http:` or `https:` protocol but never calls `isPrivateHost()`. The `/api/crawl` endpoint has no URL validation at all. An attacker can scrape `http://127.0.0.1:3000`, `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/` (AWS metadata), or any other internal service and get the HTML content returned in the response. ```javascript // Line 63-95 — /api/scrape has protocol check but no isPrivateHost call app.post("/api/scrape", async (req, res) => { // ... validates protocol ... // Missing: if (isPrivateHost(url)) return res.status(403)... const result = await scrapeUrl(url, useApi); ``` **Fix:** Call `isPrivateHost(url)` in both `/api/scrape` and `/api/crawl` handlers, and reject private addresses with a 403 response. Also validate URLs discovered during crawling before following them. ``` [HIGH-2] Crawl follows redirects to internal hosts without SSRF validation File: /Users/robinsonchan/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox/.claude/worktrees/heuristic-curran/scraper-poc/scraper.js:70-77 ``` **Issue:** The `fetchDirect` function uses `maxRedirects: 5`, which means an attacker-controlled external page could issue an HTTP redirect to `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/` or `http://127.0.0.1:xxxx/`, and axios will follow it. The same applies to `fetchCss` and `fetchViaScraperApi`. None of these validate the final redirected URL. **Fix:** Use an axios interceptor or `beforeRedirect` callback (available in axios >=1.3) to validate each redirect target against `isPrivateHost` before following it. ``` [HIGH-3] No rate limiting on any endpoint File: /Users/robinsonchan/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox/.claude/worktrees/heuristic-curran/scraper-poc/server.js (entire file) ``` **Issue:** There is no rate limiting on `/api/scrape`, `/api/crawl`, or `/api/download`. The crawl endpoint is especially dangerous since each request can trigger up to 20 outbound HTTP requests (with the `maxPages` cap). An attacker can weaponize this server to launch distributed scraping attacks or DDoS third-party websites. **Fix:** Add rate limiting middleware (e.g., `express-rate-limit`) with appropriate thresholds for each endpoint. The crawl endpoint should have stricter limits. ``` [HIGH-4] No response size limit on fetched HTML content File: /Users/robinsonchan/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox/.claude/worktrees/heuristic-curran/scraper-poc/scraper.js:60-64, 70-77 ``` **Issue:** Both `fetchViaScraperApi` and `fetchDirect` fetch the entire response body into memory without any size limit. A malicious or very large page could return gigabytes of data, causing the Node.js process to run out of memory and crash. ```javascript // Line 71 — no maxContentLength const res = await axios.get(url, { headers: DEFAULT_HEADERS, timeout: 20_000, maxRedirects: 5, // Missing: maxContentLength: 10 * 1024 * 1024 }); ``` **Fix:** Add `maxContentLength` (e.g., `10 * 1024 * 1024` for 10MB) to all axios `get` calls in `fetchDirect`, `fetchViaScraperApi`, and `fetchCss`. ``` [HIGH-5] .env file parsing does not trim quotes — environment variables may contain literal quotes File: /Users/robinsonchan/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox/.claude/worktrees/heuristic-curran/scraper-poc/server.js:19-27 ``` **Issue:** The manual `.env` parser splits on `=` and joins the remainder, but does not strip surrounding quotes. A common `.env` convention is `SCRAPERAPI_KEY="sk-abc123"`, which would set the value to `"sk-abc123"` (with literal quote characters), causing API authentication to fail silently with confusing errors. ```javascript // Line 22 — no quote stripping process.env[k] = v.join("="); // If .env has: KEY="value", process.env.KEY becomes '"value"' ``` **Fix:** Strip surrounding single/double quotes from the value: `v.join("=").replace(/^(['"])(.*)\1$/, '$2')`. Alternatively, use the `dotenv` package which handles all edge cases correctly. --- ### MEDIUM Issues ``` [MEDIUM-1] extractCssProp is vulnerable to regex injection from CSS content File: /Users/robinsonchan/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox/.claude/worktrees/heuristic-curran/scraper-poc/scraper.js:306-309 ``` **Issue:** The `prop` parameter is interpolated into a regex without escaping. While currently only called with hardcoded property names (`font-family`, `font-weight`, etc.), this is fragile.
